C-42.Name: GitHub presence refresh and an honest "two editions" comparison (App Store vs Homebrew/direct download)
C-42.Summary: The GitHub repo still says "11 MB, 61 MB RAM", "beta" and "Status v2.1.8-beta", has no social preview, no What's New, no contributor files, and its homepage points to GitHub itself. Bring it to the new brand and to verified numbers, and explain — on our own channels only — what the Homebrew/direct-download edition adds over the App Store edition without breaking App Store rules.

Problem.Description: User 2026-10-15: «ревижн материалов на гите … чтобы там тоже всё красиво было»; «напрашивается отдельный раздел, чем ДМГ версия богаче апсторовской (только так, чтобы не нарушить там ничего)».

Goals.R-1: README in the brand: cover image, "What's new in 2.3", verified numbers (window ≈0.4 s, ≈30 MB on disk, ≈310 MB with WebKit; measured 2026-10-15), install (App Store / Homebrew / Windows), agent setup, comparison matrix as on the site, store frames as screenshots, badges fixed (no beta, no 11 MB / 61 MB).
Goals.R-2: Repo About: new description and topics, homepage = https://mark.xronocode.com; a 1280×640 social-preview image (uploaded by the owner in Settings — the API cannot set it).
Goals.R-3: Contributor files: CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CHANGELOG.md (from release notes), issue templates (bug / feature) and a PR template; Discussions on if the owner agrees.
Goals.R-4: Release notes: a user-facing "What's new" section on v2.3.0 above the automated block (AGENTS.md release step 6).
Goals.R-5: "Two editions, same editor" section on the site (C-35 install section + FAQ), in README ("Editions") and in the docs (guide/editions): a neutral, factual table. Desktop edition only, verified in code on 2026-10-15 (m048 build mode and app-store cfg gates): Pandoc export (DOCX, ODT, EPUB… when pandoc is installed), insert screenshot (screencapture), set Mark as the default Markdown app, Diff against the last git commit (both editions read a .before file), the local live server for agents (m045 HTTP endpoint; the base for MCP C-25), the in-app updater, Windows builds. App Store edition: Apple-reviewed, sandboxed, updates and installs through the App Store. Everything else is the same editor. FAQ explains why: the App Store sandbox does not allow running other programs (git, pandoc, screencapture) or the local server.
Goals.R-6: App Store compliance: the App Store build, its listing, screenshots and app preview never mention or link the other edition and show only features present in the App Store build; unavailable features stay hidden in the App Store build (as today), never greyed out with a "get the other version" prompt.

G2.Title: README rewrite + editions section + docs page

C-42.Dependencies: C-35 (site uses the same editions table); C-43 and the App Store gap items below reduce the table over time.

Constraints.Constraint: Every number fact-checked against a dated measurement; App Store build, listing and preview never reference the other edition.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Changing what the App Store build can do (tracked separately).

OpenQuestions.Q-1: Resolved 2026-10-15: share enabled in the App Store build (C-44); the live server stays desktop-only (App Review comment); Diff snapshots (C-43) work in both editions.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: No outdated number or "beta" anywhere on the repo page; the editions table matches the m048 build-mode flags; nothing in the App Store build or listing references the other edition.

AffectedAreas.Bundle: README.md, .github/*, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CHANGELOG.md, site/guide/editions.md, repo settings

C-42.VerificationIntent: Link check, fact check of every number against the 2026-10-15 measurements, a test that the editions table lists exactly the m048 desktop-only flags.

Approval.ApprovedBy: user (2026-10-15): «1» (yes to C-42); Discussions stay off for now
Approval.ApprovalScope: G1–G3. Discussions off. The live server stays desktop-only (App Store gate, see C-44).
